svg.desc: Two analytic density shapes, both mean zero and variance one: the symmetric Laplace law (E minus E prime) divided by square root of two, and the centred exponential E minus one. Among centred log-concave laws the smallest Lp to L2 ratio is attained by Laplace for 1<p<p*, and by centred exponential for p*<p<2; both families attain it at p*, approximately 1.682457208455. For p>2 the centred exponential instead maximises the ratio. At p=2 every admissible law has ratio one. Reflections are included. Curves are sampled from exact analytic formulas for illustration, not certificate data; displayed tails are truncated. The regime arrangement is not a linear exponent scale.
